cards.name: Envelope Presets
cards.id: Draw/Envelope Presets.env#Envelope Presets
cards.summary: The envelope preset library file (Envelope Presets.env, about 3.7 KB, a binary list of shapes whose entry names were not decoded). The thumbnail is a script application, not a shipped preview: Shape.CreateEnvelope(PresetIndex = 1 to 6) on six orange-and-blue checkerboard squares. It shows six outcomes: a barrel or lens bulge with pointed left and right tips; a parallelogram leaning right; a parallelogram leaning left; two squares that look unchanged; and a round, ball-like circle. Cell order is assumed to follow the index order, which is not confirmed.
use_for: browsing the stock envelope shapes before picking one in the Envelope tool
knowing what Shape.CreateEnvelope(PresetIndex) gives for indexes 1 to 6
wrapping art into a lens, slant or ball shape
avoid: Treating it as one preset: it is the library holding several shapes; pick the single shape you want from the Envelope tool's preset list.
Assuming the property-bar list order: the harvest found that PresetIndex does not follow it.
Two of the six outcomes look unchanged on a checker square; check the result before relying on an index.
cards.applies_to: one vector object (closed shape, curve or text) selected with the Envelope tool; each library entry wraps the object into its outline as a live envelope
cards.how_to_apply: Toolbox > Effect Tools > Envelope (Automation.InvokeItem("1f16cb33-9819-4fa7-a3cd-5c4d61ba2db2")): select the object and choose an entry from the preset list on the property bar. Script: Shape.CreateEnvelope(PresetIndex = 1 to 6, Mode, KeepLines) is how the thumbnail was made; the library file is Draw/Envelope Presets.env in the CorelDRAW install folder.

verified.note: Script render of indexes 1-6 on checker squares: lens bulge with pointed side tips, parallelogram leaning right, parallelogram leaning left, two unchanged squares, circle, as described; this order conflicts with the failed-render note (index 3 = circle), so the mapping stays unconfirmed.

cards.name: GIF 128 dithered
cards.id: Custom Data/Export/GIF 128 dithered.xml#GIF 128 dithered
cards.summary: Export preset for a GIF: an optimized palette of 128 colours, Floyd-Steinberg dithering at amount 100, transparency on, antialiasing on, not interlaced, white matte. No look of its own: it sets file-format options, so there is no thumbnail.
use_for: small web graphics with soft gradients or photo areas
keeping file size down: fewer colours (128) means a smaller file
legacy web and email graphics that need a GIF
avoid: Photos and smooth gradients in full quality: 256 colours at most, so banding or speckle shows; use JPEG or PNG 24-bit.
Semi-transparent edges: GIF transparency is on/off only, so soft shadows get a hard halo; export PNG 24-bit instead.
Flat-colour logos where dither noise would look dirty: use a 'no dither' variant.
cards.applies_to: an export operation, not an object: it sets the file-format options for the bitmap that is exported from the document, a page or the selection
cards.how_to_apply: File > Export For > Web (Automation.InvokeItem("4b3e61ff-29f6-dda5-412a-066817e75008")): pick 'GIF 128 dithered' from the preset list in the dialog. This is the usual route for these presets; the harvest read the preset's XML file (Custom Data/Export/GIF 128 dithered.xml in the CorelDRAW install folder) but did not walk the dialog, so the exact list is unconfirmed. Script: no call that loads a preset by name was found; set the same values on IGIFFilterSettings (Palette, NumColors, Dithering, DitheringAmount, Transparency, Interlaced) from the export-tool type library (not tested by the harvest).

verified.note: No thumbnail (export settings, not visual); every stated value checked against the preset XML file and matches.
